officialTitle: First-Line Lorlatinib or Crizotinib in Advanced ALK-Positive Lung Cancer

design.blinding: PFS by blinded independent central review
design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: We conducted a global, randomized, phase 3 trial comparing lorlatinib with crizotinib in 296 patients with advanced-positive NSCLC who had received no previous systemic treatment for metastatic disease.
design.notes: Primary publication was a planned interim analysis.

clinicalQuestion: Is the third-generation ALK inhibitor lorlatinib superior to crizotinib as first-line therapy for advanced ALK-positive NSCLC?

pico.population: Advanced ALK-positive NSCLC without prior systemic therapy for metastatic disease
pico.outcomes: Primary: BICR PFS. Secondary: ORR, intracranial response

publications.title: First-Line Lorlatinib or Crizotinib in Advanced-Positive Lung Cancer.
publications.label: Planned interim analysis

publications.title: Lorlatinib Versus Crizotinib in Patients With Advanced-Positive Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: 5-Year Outcomes From the Phase III CROWN Study.
publications.label: 5-year update (post hoc)

outcomes.endpointLabel: PFS by blinded independent central review
outcomes.sourceQuote: The percentage of patients who were alive without disease progression at 12 months was 78% (95% confidence interval [CI], 70 to 84) in the lorlatinib group and 39% (95% CI, 30 to 48) in the crizotinib group (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.28; 95% CI, 0.19 to 0.41; P<0.001).
An objective response occurred in 76% (95% CI, 68 to 83) of the patients in the lorlatinib group and 58% (95% CI, 49 to 66) of those in the crizotinib group

among those with measurable brain metastases, 82% (95% CI, 57 to 96) and 23% (95% CI, 5 to 54), respectively, had an intracranial response, and 71% of the patients who received lorlatinib had an intracranial complete response.

With a median follow-up for PFS of 60.2 and 55.1 months, respectively, median PFS was not reached (NR [95% CI, 64.3 to NR]) with lorlatinib and 9.1 months (95% CI, 7.4 to 10.9) with crizotinib (hazard ratio [HR], 0.19 [95% CI, 0.13 to 0.27]); 5-year PFS was 60% (95% CI, 51 to 68) and 8% (95% CI, 3 to 14), respectively.
Median time to intracranial progression was NR (95% CI, NR to NR) with lorlatinib and 16.4 months (95% CI, 12.7 to 21.9) with crizotinib (HR, 0.06 [95% CI, 0.03 to 0.12]).

safety.description: Grade 3 or 4 adverse events (mainly altered lipid levels)
safety.sourceQuote: Lorlatinib was associated with more grade 3 or 4 adverse events (mainly altered lipid levels) than crizotinib (in 72% vs. 56%).
Discontinuation of treatment because of adverse events occurred in 7% and 9% of the patients, respectively.

safety.description: Most common adverse events with lorlatinib
safety.experimentalValue: Hyperlipidaemia, oedema, weight gain, peripheral neuropathy, cognitive effects
safety.sourceQuote: The most common adverse events with lorlatinib were hyperlipidemia, edema, increased weight, peripheral neuropathy, and cognitive effects.

limitations: 5-year analysis is post hoc and investigator-assessed
OS data not reported in these abstracts

clinicalImplications.text: Supports lorlatinib as a first-line ALK TKI with durable systemic and intracranial control, requiring proactive management of lipid and CNS adverse effects.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Counsel on mood/cognitive effects and monitor lipids when starting lorlatinib.

curation.notes: Numbers transcribed from PubMed abstracts of PMID 33207094 (interim) and PMID 38819031 (5-year update). Doses from the 5-year update abstract.
